title: Closing EXP-067's three named gaps: flat abstention, single-child navigation, and margin calibration
goal: Fix and re-measure, not just patch, the three concrete gaps named right after EXP-067: lab.common.brain's flat disambiguation branch had no abstention at all; lab.common.semantic_index.navigate_semantic could not handle a level with only one candidate; and MIN_SEMANTIC_MARGIN=0.03 was a single first measurement, not a validated constant.
method: Part A: brain.reason run on EXP-058/060's integrated fixture (2 regression cases) plus a new off-topic case and a new flat-document paraphrase case, through the new dual lexical+semantic signal logic. Part B: navigate_semantic run on a single-level, single-child tree, with a genuine ask and an off-topic ask, to exercise the new dense-floor fallback. Part C: margin sweep across 3 independently-worded tree fixtures (72 leaves each), each with an exact-wording ask, a paraphrase ask, and 3 off-topic asks, collecting the top1-vs-runner-up margin at every level visited (ignoring abstention, for measurement purposes) to check whether MIN_SEMANTIC_MARGIN actually separates genuine matches from real noise.
results_prose: Part A (flat disambiguation, brain.py): 3/4 end-to-end correct -- the two EXP-060 regression cases hold and the off-topic ask now abstains instead of guessing. The new paraphrase case is a mixed result worth stating precisely rather than rounding off: disambiguation itself resolved the right group ('A', correct), but the overall case still came back 'inconclusive' -- the failure is downstream of the fix just made, in brain.py's _wants_identity/_wants_total keyword checks, which don't recognize this paraphrase's intent wording ('take-home pay', 'extra payout') the way they recognize 'name'/'address'/'total' literally, so it falls through to the single-slot lookup extractor and finds no single-span answer. Part B (single-child fallback, navigate_semantic): genuine ask proceeded, off-topic ask correctly abstained (reason: only one section candidate and it scored at the dense-similarity floor (dense 0.0000 < 1e-09) -- no margin was computable to check instead). Part C (margin sweep, 3 fixtures x (1 exact + 1 paraphrase + 3 off-topic) asks, 2 levels each): genuine-match margins range down to 0.0031, noise margins range up to 0.0631; the two populations are NOT cleanly separable. The current MIN_SEMANTIC_MARGIN=0.03 is NOT safely inside the measured gap.
conclusion: All three gaps named after EXP-067 were addressed and re-measured rather than assumed fixed, and one new, more important finding came out of that re-measurement than the three fixes themselves. Flat disambiguation now abstains correctly on the off-topic case and still answers both EXP-060 regression cases, using the identical dual-signal (lexical floor + semantic margin, independent checks that must agree) design EXP-067 validated for hierarchical navigation -- the same mechanism now covers both branches of lab.common.brain. The disambiguation fix itself worked even on the paraphrase case (it resolved the correct group); what still fails downstream of it is a *separate*, pre-existing issue this exploration exposed rather than caused: brain.py's _wants_identity and _wants_total signal detectors are themselves literal keyword checks ('name' + 'address', a fixed list of total-cue words), so a paraphrased ask can pass disambiguation correctly and still get no answer because the intent-detection step never recognized what kind of question it was. That's a fourth, newly-identified gap, not one of the three this exploration set out to fix. The single-candidate gap in navigate_semantic is closed by falling back to the TF-IDF dense floor specifically where a margin can't be computed, reusing lab.common.nested_index's already-measured constant rather than inventing a new number. the margin sweep found the two populations are NOT cleanly separable (min genuine 0.0031 <= max noise 0.0631) -- meaning no single fixed threshold can be fully trusted across different vocabularies, a real limitation to flag rather than paper over with a confident-sounding constant.
scale_down: 3 margin-sweep fixtures, 1 single-child case, 4 flat-disambiguation cases -- enough to validate the mechanism and get a first real measurement of separability, not an exhaustive calibration.
follow_ups: New, higher-priority than the three this exploration closed: brain.py's _wants_identity/_wants_total are literal keyword checks ('name'+'address', a fixed total-cue word list) -- a paraphrased ask can pass disambiguation correctly (proven working here) and still fail because intent detection itself doesn't recognize it. The same lexical+semantic dual-signal fix just applied to disambiguation is the natural pattern to apply here too, not a keyword-list expansion.

The margin sweep found genuine-match and noise margins are NOT cleanly separable by any single global threshold across 3 fixtures and 2 levels (min genuine 0.0031 <= max noise 0.0631) -- MIN_SEMANTIC_MARGIN=0.03 is not a safe fixed constant. This is why brain.py's disambiguation never trusts the semantic margin alone -- it only acts when lexical also abstains or agrees -- but navigate_semantic's hierarchical path still uses the margin as its only signal at each level and inherits this same risk. Needs either a per-level/relative recalibration or a second corroborating signal there too, not a bigger single constant.
If MIN_SEMANTIC_MARGIN is adjusted, rerun EXP-066/067 to confirm nothing regresses.
The single-child fallback still can't catch a paraphrased ask the way the margin check can -- only exercised against an exact/off-topic pair here, not a paraphrase against a lone candidate.
models_used: bge-small-en-v1.5 for all semantic scoring (retrieval only, no generation); TF-IDF/BM25 (lab.common.index) for the lexical signal and the single-child fallback floor.
